answer.rationale: Primary supply expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so continuity is binding. Adding a second source or deferring would leave the expiring primary uncovered (c5 applied only to non-critical spend). Switching would hit the 18% cut on unit price (current quote; c2 claims quick onboarding) but would raise delivery risk on a no-buffer line; that onboarding claim is the one memory worth verifying. Incumbent renewal has held integration and deliveries (c1). Past renewal benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and terms (c4) and multi-year volume structure cut unit cost without shrinking scope (c6). Use the low-cost quote as the benchmark and negotiate the incumbent renewal to pursue the spend cut without a supplier cutover.
